audit_findings.title: Finite-life catalog amortization may be economic depletion
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.556 million FY2026 amortization added back against $39.4 million anchor OE; sustaining-depletion adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A sustaining catalog-investment or economic-depletion charge would reduce anchor OE and every projected and terminal cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: Music catalogs acquired during the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025 were determined to have a useful life of 30 years .
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved economic-cost question, not proof that accounting amortization equals depletion. It is material because the filed amortization equals 77.6% of anchor OE, while FY2026 catalog purchases were $101.601 million. Even a fraction being sustaining expenditure could materially reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $39.4 million anchor, estimate catalog revenue decay, expirations and recapture by vintage, classify catalog purchases between sustaining and expansion, and rerun all scenarios with the supported sustaining charge.

audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may require acquisition spending omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $101.601 million of FY2026 catalog purchases, equal to 2.58x the $39.4 million anchor OE; required future growth investment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition and advance spending needed to produce projected growth must reduce OE cash flows; deferred consideration alternatively enters the equity bridge as a claim.
audit_findings.evidence: Asset and company acquisitions have been our path to growth since inception.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: the filing identifies acquisitions as a path to growth and attributes revenue growth partly to acquired catalogs, while the 5% and 8% projections provide no acquisition funding. The exact correction remains unresolved because organic growth and expansion investment have not been separated.
audit_findings.action: Build an organic-versus-acquired growth bridge, quantify purchase spending, royalty advances and deferred consideration required for each scenario, and rerun base and bull cash flows after those charges.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated cash-flow adjustments
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.430 million June 2026 NCI balance and $0.415 million quarterly loss attributable to NCI; OE attribution mismatch unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Adjustments belonging to noncontrolling holders can distort parent-attributable OE; alternatively, consolidated OE requires deduction of the NCI claim in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company records a noncontrolling interest in its consolidated balance sheets and statements of operations with respect to the remaining economic interests in majority-owned subsidiaries it does not own.
audit_findings.explanation: The basis mismatch is demonstrated if parent-attributable income was combined with consolidated D&A, capital spending and other adjustments. The record does not allocate those adjustments by subsidiary, so neither direction nor materiality can be established from the small reported NCI balance alone.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsidiary-level D&A, capital expenditure, advances and other OE adjustments; calculate parent-attributable OE or value consolidated OE and separately determine the economic NCI claim.

audit_findings.title: The post-expiration warrant denominator is unresolved
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 5.8875 million shares, or 8.0% of the 73.593799 million denominator; if none were exercised, removing them raises scenario values per share by 8.7% to $7.12, $9.33 and $10.96 and buy-below to $6.53
audit_findings.mechanism: Expired or unexercised warrants must leave fully diluted shares; exercised warrants require matching new shares and exercise proceeds in the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Warrants will expire on July 28, 2026, which is five years after the completion of the Business Combination, or earlier upon redemption or liquidation.
audit_findings.explanation: Including warrants after their filed July 28, 2026 expiration is a demonstrated denominator error. The final exercise mix remains unresolved, but the maximum share effect is large enough to affect per-share conclusions, especially the narrow bull-case premium to the $9.74 price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the warrant agent's final expiration, exercise, cashless-exercise and redemption report, then rerun per-share values with the resulting shares and proceeds treated consistently.

audit_findings.title: Prior-period royalty revenue may inflate the FY2026 anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.947 million of revenue, equal to 1.1% of FY2026 revenue and 4.9% of the $39.4 million anchor OE; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring favorable royalty true-up would be removed from anchor revenue together with its associated royalty costs and taxes before forecasting OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company recognized revenue of $ 1,947,135 and $ 4,382,721 from performance obligations satisfied in previous periods for the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The prior-period revenue is filed, but the record does not show whether it is a discrete favorable true-up or routine lag settlement already offset by current-period estimates. Consequently, an anchor adjustment is possible but not demonstrated, and its after-cost OE magnitude cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the amount to prior accrual estimates, cash receipts, royalty costs and recurring lag patterns; if discrete, normalize anchor OE and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stated null perimeter omits a completed post-year-end acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.893 million purchase consideration, equal to 1.22% of bear, 0.93% of base and 0.79% of bull equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Post-acquisition earnings increase OE, while associated financing interest reduces OE; acquired cash, consideration and liabilities affect the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Viral Wave Acquisition closed on April 7, 2026 following required regulatory approvals and the Company will account for the transaction as a business combination in accordance with ASC Topic 805, Business Combinations .
audit_findings.explanation: The March earnings and June balance-sheet perimeters are demonstrably inconsistent. However, the entire filed purchase consideration is only 0.8%-1.2% of scenario equity values, providing a concrete basis that this acquisition alone is not reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion. Direction is mixed because acquired earnings are omitted while post-acquisition financing costs are also absent from the anchor.
audit_findings.action: For consistency, incorporate Viral Wave's April 7-to-June operating results, purchase accounting and financing interest into a June run-rate rerun, or restore both OE and bridge to the pre-acquisition perimeter.
